newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson Land expected to post strong interim net.
newsitem.headline: Henderson Land expected to post strong interim net.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, one of Hong Kong's most profitable property developers, is set to show a strong rise in interim net profit after a busy period of property sales, analysts said on Monday.

"Among the big three developers - Cheung Kong, Sun Hung Kai and Henderson - Henderson is the one that had the most residential property units for sale last year," said Ricky Tam, research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
He expected the company to post at least 20 percent net profit growth when it reports its results for the six months ended December 31, 1996, on Wednesday.
It had net profit of HK$4.01 billion or earnings per share of HK$2.51 for the same period the previous year.
"About 95 percent of their operating profit comes from developments for sale with the balance from rental," said Michael Leary, senior property analyst at Lehman Brothers.
He forecast full year earnings per share of HK$6.11 compared with HK$5.16.
Analysts said the main contributors to earnings growth should be Henderson Land's Metro City and Tolo Place developments in the New Territories.
Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities, said Henderson Land had bought the Metro City site in Tseung Kwan O at a low cost and its profit margin was extremely high.
"It is possibly one of the most profitable among major developers," he said.
Chan forecast interim net profit of about HK$5.2 billion.

"Metro City accounts for roughly 49 percent of development earnings - so about HK$2.5 billion," said Carol Lai, research manager at SocGen-Crosby Securities. "Tolo Place, they presold about 64 percent, so that accounts for about HK$1.15 billion."
She forecast interim net profit of HK$4.59 billion, which did not include any possible exceptionals.
"I think the wild card is in the booking of exceptional profits. During the spin-off of Henderson China the company managed to secure an exceptional gain of about HK$2 billion," said Lai.
Henderson Land's China property arm Henderson China Holdings Ltd listed last March in Hong Kong.
Lai said Henderson Land had room to book HK$1.4 billion from the spin-off after booking HK$664 million last year.
"You have got just over HK$1 billion coming from Henderson China most of which will be booked in the second half of 1997," added Leary.

He said solid earnings growth from the major property developers should help improve sentiment towards the property stocks, "particularly after they have been knocked so significantly over the first quarter".
Henderson Land shares closed at HK$64.50 on Monday, up HK$1.50. "At HK$64.50, the stock is trading at 10.4 times 1997 earnings," said Lai.
"We have been recommending a buy on Henderson Land and at these levels the stock is definitely looking quite attractive."
But Lai was not so positive on Henderson Investment Ltd which is 66 percent-owned by Henderson Land.
"We are looking at an earnings decline of 35 percent, the reason being that the company really has not secured much property sales in the first half," she said.
Henderson Investment, which is also due to report interim results on Wednesday, posted net profit for the six months ended December 31, 1995 of HK$1.34 billion.
